profile.headline: Software Developer at Capital One
profile.summary:
Experienced graduate student with a demonstrated history of working in academia and industry. Experienced in programming Languages & Technologies such as Java 8, Spring( SpringBoot, SpringData), OOP, SQL/Postgres, Angular/Typescript, Python, C++
As well as experience in developer tools such as Git/Github, Agile/Scrum practices, Splunk, JSON, NPM, IntelliJ, Tomcat/Apache, Docker, AWS, Jenkins CI/CD Pipeline, PagerDuty

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
● Develop, maintain, and support both new and pre-existing full stack applications and Java APIs
● Backend Java development that runs on a Spring Boot Framework. Also redeveloping an existing Java orchestration layer that supports the CapitalOne.com website
● Frontend Web interfaces in Angular/Angular7 that is seen and used by millions of customers
● Middleware technology to connect it all together using AWS, Docker, and Jenkins pipelines for
deployment and Database interactions in Postgres

positions.title: Graduate Teaching Assistant
positions.description:
In this role I work on a team of several undergraduate and graduate TA's, as well as several professor to teach a class of approximately 50-75 students basic engineering skills such as circuitry and programming.

My responsibilities for this role are similar to my responsibilities of being an undergrad TA.

positions.title: Student Summer Intern
positions.description: As an intern in the firmware security department my summer assignment was implementing two factor authentication system for the printers. Once my assignment was in a stable state I was able to package my project and send it to the corporate IT team. The work I performed served as a proof of concept that this authentication system could and will work on the printers as well as be expanded to fit future corporate needs.

positions.title: AYPT (Student Intern)
positions.description:
In my time as an intern I worked in both the marketing and firmware departments in Lexmark. 

As a marketing intern I worked in competitive intelligence where I was responsible for interacting with internal, as well as external, customers to accomplish and meet customer needs in a timely manner, support the marketing team by providing researched information of how Lexmark devices stacked against competitive devices, and more.

As a firmware intern I worked with an embedded frameworks team where I was responsible for researching ways to automate tests on physical and virtual printer interfaces using a variety of internal and external automation tools such as Sikuli and Lettuce to name a few. I was also responsible for determining a way to integrate my solution into the company-wide testing infrastructure.

positions.title: Undergraduate Teaching Assistant
positions.description:
In this role I taught the lab section of an introductory course to C++. During these lab sections I would help the students take what they learned in lecture and apply it to the weekly lab assignment. 

My responsibilities for this role were grading, running weekly 2-hour lab sections, communicating with students both in and out of class, being a knowledge source for student questions and debugging issues, attending staff meetings, and more. Some semesters I was responsible for holding office hours where students could meet with me and get any extra help over the class material. Class sizes ranged from about 20 to 40 students a semester.

positions.title: Undergraduate Research Assistant
positions.description:
Provided assistance, contribution, and collaboration to a team working on Dr. Jerzy Jaromczyk’s research project of Fungal Endophytes Genomes; pertaining to analyzing genomes, importing and developing a database, along with writing unique Perl and Bash scripts for automating the process. Automating the process has saved hundred of man hours in processing genome data. 

Participation in this research has lead to several conference and symposium appearances, both national and regional, as well as a publication in which I have been cited on entitled:Automating deployment of several GBrowse instances (April 2014).

positions.title: Shift Manager
positions.description: As a Shift Manager I ensured that everything was under control during my shift and made sure that customers had a satisfactory experience. My typical responsibilities included overseeing all operations from greeting customers to the quality and speed of service in the restaurant, handling resturant finances, orchestrating truck deliveries and more. Additional responsibilities included overseeing adequate maintenance of equipment, keeping track of inventory and monitoring the quality of products supplied. On average, I managed a team of 10 to 20 people per shift.

honors.title: GEM Fellowship
honors.description: A network of leading corporations, government laboratories, top universities, and top research institutions that enables qualified students from underrepresented communities to pursue graduate education in applied science and engineering by funding their graduate degree program.
honors.issuer: Issued by The National GEM Consortium · Jun 2016

honors.title: Lyman T. Johnson Fellowship
honors.description: Competitive fellowship award made on the basis of GPA, GRE or GMAT scores, letters of recommendation and continuation of the University's compelling interest in the educational benefits of diversity.
honors.issuer: Issued by University of Kentucky · Jun 2016
